    "claim_assessments": [
      {
        "id": "C1",
        "text": "在PFI精磨过程中，softwood fiber的湿纸幅强度相较hardwood fiber出现了更显著的提高。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "E14",
        "basis": {
          "type": "reference_evidence",
          "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying."
    ]
  }
}

原107块小节补全 · 要点 2/3；边界 1/2

为确定拟合峰位，作者将光谱在1016 cm−1归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线，从二阶导数谱按不同H-bond归属区域读取波数。 [1]
非线性拟合的FT-IR波段为3000–3700 cm−1，采用Gaussian函数，并在Peakfit 4.12软件中完成。 [1]
依据二阶导数确定的峰位，作者将3000–3700 cm−1的羟基谱带解卷积为四个主要谱带，分别对应O(6)H···O(3′) inter-molecular、O(3)H···O(5) intra-molecular、O(2)H···O(6) intra-molecular以及free OH(2) and OH(6)。 [3]
不同氢键的相对含量口径是各解卷积谱带的面积占比，Table 2列出三种H-bonds和free OH的相对含量。 [3]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Finally, the data and curves obtained using nonlinear fitting for softwood fibers is shown in Table 2a and Figure 7, and the results of hardwood fibers can be seen in Table 2b and Figure S3.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be <sup>For</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>content</sup> <sup>of</sup> <sup>O(6)H O(3′)</sup> <sup>inter-molecular</sup> <sup>H-bonds</sup> <sup>of</sup> <sup>softwood</sup> <sup>fiber,</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>trend</sup> <sup>can</sup> <sup>be</sup>divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds of <sup>with</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>revolutions</sup> <sup>increasing</sup> <sup>from</sup> <sup>8000</sup> <sup>r</sup> <sup>to</sup> <sup>16,000</sup> <sup>r.</sup> <sup>Regarding</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>O(6)H O(3′)</sup> <sup>H-bonds</sup> <sup>of</sup>hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1)."

仅删回退额外邻块 · 要点 2/3；边界 1/2

FT-IR光谱在1016 cm⁻¹处归一化，并用Savitzky–Golay算法获得导数曲线；各氢键组分的波数取自第二导数谱中对应不同氢键归属的区域。 [1]
对3000–3700 cm⁻¹的FT-IR谱区使用Gaussian函数，在Peakfit 4.12软件中进行非线性拟合。 [1]
根据上述峰位，将3000–3700 cm⁻¹的羟基谱带去卷积为四个主要谱带。 [3]
各拟合谱带的归属包括：3580–3550 cm⁻¹为free OH(2)和OH(6)，3455–3410 cm⁻¹为O(2)H···O(6)分子内氢键，3375–3340 cm⁻¹为O(3)H···O(5)分子内氢键，3310–3230 cm⁻¹为cellulose I中的O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键。 [3]
不同氢键的相对含量按各拟合谱带的面积占比分别计算。 [3]
结果表中给出三种氢键O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5)、O(2)H···O(6)以及free OH(2)和OH(6)的相对含量百分比，并列出拟合的r²值。 [3]

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. FT-IR Analysis\n[原文]\nTHE FT-IR spectra were recorded on solid samples in KBr pellets by means of an FT-IR Bruker Vertex 70 spectrometer (Karlsruhe, Germany). Unrefined and refined fibers were smashed into powder between 40 and 60 mesh. Subsequently, the powder sample of each species (5 mg) was dispersed in a matrix of highly pure KBr (500 mg). O(6)H···O(3′) 分子间氢键的红外区间约为 3310–3230 cm⁻¹。 [1]
O(3)H···O(5) 分子内氢键的红外区间约为 3375–3340 cm⁻¹。 [1]
O(2)H···O(6) 分子内氢键的红外区间约为 3455–3410 cm⁻¹。 [1]
这三种氢键的对应峰位分别约为 3227、3346 和 3452 cm⁻¹。 [1]

FT-IR Analysis\n[原文]\nTHE FT-IR spectra were recorded on solid samples in KBr pellets by means of an FT-IR Bruker Vertex 70 spectrometer (Karlsruhe, Germany). Unrefined and refined fibers were smashed into powder between 40 and 60 mesh. Subsequently, the powder sample of each species (5 mg) was dispersed in a matrix of highly pure KBr (500 mg). The spectral was recorded by averaging 64 recordings and at a resolution of 4 $\\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ with transmission mode from 4000 cm<sup>−1</sup> to $4 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ . 原107块小节补全 · 要点 3/3；边界 2/2

论文报告软木纤维和硬木纤维中O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5)、O(2)H···O(6)三种氢键的峰位置在整个打浆过程中几乎保持恒定，由相应公式计算得到的氢键能和氢键距离因而未发生变化。 [1]
论文摘要指出，打浆后纤维素多晶型、氢键距离与氢键能量几乎不变，但结晶度、微晶尺寸以及各类氢键的含量随打浆而改变。 [3]
表2数据显示，软木纤维O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键的相对含量随打浆波动，从0转的28.23%降至16000转时的23.56%。 [1]
总体而言，软木纤维和硬木纤维的O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量分别下降了16.54%和5.91%。 [1]
这种减少可能归因于PFI打浆机械作用下纤维素分子链间的断裂，与内外部细纤维化密切相关；同时含量也存在增加，说明既有氢键断裂也有氢键生成。 [1]
因此氢键能和氢键距离不变只反映氢键强度参数稳定，不能据此认为打浆对氢键网络没有影响，因为氢键含量已经发生改变。 [1] [3]

  "task_id": "PFI2-020",
  "answer": "论文报告软木纤维和硬木纤维中O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5)、O(2)H···O(6)三种氢键的峰位置在整个打浆过程中几乎保持恒定，由相应公式计算得到的氢键能和氢键距离因而未发生变化。 [1]\n论文摘要指出，打浆后纤维素多晶型、氢键距离与氢键能量几乎不变，但结晶度、微晶尺寸以及各类氢键的含量随打浆而改变。 [3]\n表2数据显示，软木纤维O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键的相对含量随打浆波动，从0转的28.23%降至16000转时的23.56%。 [1]\n总体而言，软木纤维和硬木纤维的O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量分别下降了16.54%和5.91%。 [1]\n这种减少可能归因于PFI打浆机械作用下纤维素分子链间的断裂，与内外部细纤维化密切相关；同时含量也存在增加，说明既有氢键断裂也有氢键生成。 [1]\n因此氢键能和氢键距离不变只反映氢键强度参数稳定，不能据此认为打浆对氢键网络没有影响，因为氢键含量已经发生改变。 [1] [3]",

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages."
    ]
  }
}

仅删回退额外邻块 · 要点 3/3；边界 2/2

论文报告PFI打浆过程中O(6)H···O(3′)、O(3)H···O(5)和O(2)H···O(6)氢键的峰位几乎不变，因此由公式计算出的氢键能量和氢键距离基本不变。 [1]
同一论文明确指出，打浆过程中晶区指数、微晶尺寸以及各类氢键的含量会随打浆发生变化。 [3]
表中数据表明氢键相对含量并非恒定，例如软木纤维O(6)H···O(3′)氢键含量从0转的28.23%变为16,000转的23.56%，其间还有升降波动。 [1]
作者把O(6)H···O(3′)氢键总量下降归因于PFI打浆机械作用造成纤维素分子链断裂，并与内细纤维化和外细纤维化相关，同时指出过程中也有新氢键形成。 [1]
因此，“氢键能量和距离基本不变”只能说明既有类型氢键的强度与几何参数较稳定，不能推出打浆对氢键网络整体没有影响，因为氢键含量和超分子结构仍然改变。 [1] [3]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.",

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury",

FT-IR Analysis\n[原文]\nTHE FT-IR spectra were recorded on solid samples in KBr pellets by means of an FT-IR Bruker Vertex 70 spectrometer (Karlsruhe, Germany). Unrefined and refined fibers were smashed into powder between 40 and 60 mesh. Subsequently, the powder sample of each species (5 mg) was dispersed in a matrix of highly pure KBr (500 mg). The spectral was recorded by averaging 64 recordings and at a resolution of 4 $\\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ with transmission mode from 4000 cm<sup>−1</sup> to $4 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ . The results were made on the average spectrum that was obtained from five recordings.\n\nThe energy of the H-bonding $\\mathrm { E _ { H } }$ for several OH stretching bands was calculated while using Equation (4) [13].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. The wavenumbers of H-bonding components are taken from second-derivative spectra according to regions that are assigned to various H-bonds. Nonlinear fitting of the FT-IR spectral region from $\\bar { 3 } 0 0 0 \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ to $3 7 0 0 ~ \\mathrm { c m } ^ { - \\mathrm { 1 } }$ was carried out with Gaussian function in Peakfit 4.12 software (SeaSolve Software Inc., Framingham, MA, USA). The Pearson correlation coeficients were evaluated between the CI and content of various H-bonds, with a statistically significant p-value of <0.05, while using Spss 25.0 statistics software (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).",

Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages."

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying.",

The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).",

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. The result is consistent with the report of Haigler & Roberts [26], which shows that there might be two microfibrils associated along part of their length.\n\n4.1 nm\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nFigure 5. Cross-section model of cellulose crystallite for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers.",

Conclusions\n[原文]\nupramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.PFI refining acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of thethe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Conclusions\n[原文]\nupramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.PFI refining acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of thethe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4.       "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

      "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKunpeng Li, Lihong Zhao \\* and Beihai He\n\nState Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering, South China University of Technology, 381 Wushan Rd., Tianhe District, Guangzhou 510640, China; felikp@mail.scut.edu.cn (K.L.); ppebhhe@scut.edu.cn (B.H.) \\* Correspondence: zhaolh@scut.edu.cn\n\nReceived: 17 November 2020; Accepted: 2 December 2020; Published: 4 December 2020\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nKeywords: natural cellulosic fibers; mechanical refining; Crystallinity; Crystallite size; Hydrogen bonds",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Regarding the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds of <sup>with</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>revolutions</sup> <sup>increasing</sup> <sup>from</sup> <sup>8000</sup> <sup>r</sup> <sup>to</sup> <sup>16,000</sup> <sup>r.</sup> <sup>Regarding</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>O(6)H O(3′)</sup> <sup>H-bonds</sup> <sup>of</sup>hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the free OH(2) and OH(6) of softwood fiber, the relative content showed a slight increase trend in general. The enhancement of the free OH(2) and OH(6) was understandable, because there was the breakage of H-bonds among cellulosic molecules, which resulted in more extensive delamination and higher specific surface area (as shown in Figure S4 and Table S1 in Online Resource). This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Thus although there is the formation of free OH(2) and OH(6) during fibrillation, the content of the free OH(2) and OH(6) might disease; meanwhile, the content of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) or the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds might increase upon drying."

在3.4节中，针叶木的O(6)H···O(3′)分子间氢键含量与CI-XI的Pearson相关系数为0.912（p<0.05）。 [1]
同一文献摘要中，针叶木对应的Pearson相关系数写为0.888（p<0.05）。 [2]
因此，正文3.4节结果与摘要中的针叶木相关系数数值存在差异。 [1] [2]

      "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.",

However, the CI-XI and the CI-XA were correlated signif<sup>for</sup> <sup>both</sup> <sup>softwood</sup> <sup>fibers</sup> <sup>and</sup> <sup>hardwood</sup> <sup>fibers,</sup> <sup>with</sup> <sup>a</sup> <sup>correlation</sup> <sup>coefficient</sup> <sup>of</sup> <sup>0.919</sup> <sup>(p</sup> <sup><</sup> <sup>0.</sup>for hardwood fibers, respectively, which is consistent with the report of Ahvenainen et al. [25].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nFigure 4. The CI-XI (crystallinity index obtained by comparing intensity of X-ray difractometer (XRD) peaks) and CI-XA (crystallinity index obtained by comparing area of XRD peaks) for refined and unrefined samples: (a) softwood fiber and (b) hardwood fiber.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3.
